walkthroughs.body_html:
Jesus taught radical forgiveness — 'seventy-seven times' (Matthew 18:22).

The Lord's Prayer: 'Forgive us our trespasses as we forgive those who trespass against us' (Matthew 6:12).

The Qur'an says 'Repel evil with what is better' (41:34) and praises those who pardon others.

The UK abolished the death penalty for murder in 1965 (completely 1998). The Roman Catholic Church now teaches the death penalty is 'inadmissible' (Catechism, updated 2018).

Some Christians point to Genesis 9:6 to support it. In Islamic teaching, qisas (retaliation) is permitted for murder but the family can forgive (Qur'an 2:178).

Restorative justice brings offender and victim together to repair harm. Many Christians see this as embodying gospel values of forgiveness and reconciliation.

Community service, prison and fines are common UK responses. Reformation programmes (education, therapy) reflect a Christian and Islamic concern for redemption.

mcqs.q: When was UK capital punishment abolished?
How many aims of punishment are commonly listed?
What does the Abrahamic covenant in Judaism involve?
options: Being 'chosen' means Jews believe they are superior to other peoples.
The covenant means Jews must not interact with non-Jews.
The design argument proves evolution is false.
God's promise to Abraham of land, descendants and blessing, in return for faithfulness — the foundational covenant marking Jews as a covenant people with responsibilities, not privileges.

mcqs.q: What does the teleological (design) argument claim?
options: The design argument proves God created the world in seven days.
Apparent purpose, order or complexity in the universe implies an intelligent designer — Paley's watchmaker analogy is the classic example.
The design argument proves evolution is false.
Moksha is the Hindu word for heaven.

mcqs.q: How do samsara, karma and moksha fit together in Hindu thought?
options: Moksha is the Hindu word for heaven.
Samsara, karma and moksha are three separate Hindu deities.
The design argument proves evolution is false.
Samsara is the cycle of rebirth; karma is the law of action and consequence that drives rebirth; moksha is liberation from samsara — these form a connected chain, not three independent ideas.
